description: C1 infinity step 3 (bean qou-odh5). Two-pole Prony resolves the q-Borel singularity structure into an EXACT ANTIPODAL PAIR xi = +/- 2.36510358..., sum zero to 21 digits, branch-independent to 2.2e-29. This corrects step 2's reading of a 3.7e-4 'branch spread' as two nearby singularities: that was a single-pole ratio test blending one antipodal pair. The +/- matches the leading blocks B = +/- sqrt(q-1)/q. |xi| is normalisation-dependent and is NOT identified; xi_2/xi_1 = -1 is the canonical datum. Multipliers not extracted.

results.method: two-pole Prony / Hankel on c_m = b_m q^{m(m-1)/4}
results.corrects: step 2 (c3-w2-c1-qborel-singularity.witness.json) read the 3.7e-4 branch spread as two nearby singularities; it is one antipodal pair blended by a single-pole estimator

verdict: MIXED. CONFIRMED numerically: the q-Borel singularities form an exact antipodal pair, branch-independent to 2.2e-29 -- superseding step 2's 'two nearby singularities' reading. WITHDRAWN: the interpretation of that pair as the two Stokes sectors. The diagnostic shows b_(m+1)/b_m -> 9.3e-24, so the recurrence is effectively two-step, and a two-step recurrence has characteristic roots +/- sqrt(lam) -- it manufactures an antipodal pair with no Stokes content. The match to the +/- of the leading blocks was circular (even/odd decoupling and ramification index 2 are the same structure). SCOPE-(a) NEGATIVE on the Prony/ratio route to the multipliers: the alternating component is suppressed by ~1e-24, so sector information is not visible in the raw b_m. Reaching the multipliers needs theta-normalised canonical solutions in the ramified picture, which this method does not build.
scope: Separates and characterises the singularity pair. Does NOT extract the Stokes multipliers. |xi| deliberately not identified (normalisation-dependent). Numerical, no fit, nothing wired.
